edge_explainer.market_believes: A Florida insurer at the top of the cycle: peak earnings from a hurricane-free year, rates rolling over, growth stalling — take profits before the wind blows.
edge_explainer.we_believe: Mostly the same — but the biggest cost line just got cut 15% with MORE protection, locked for 12 months, and the phase-in of rate givebacks lags by 2-4 quarters. We're paid a real margin bulge to hold a diversified, well-reinsured book through a season forecast below-normal, with one event capped near 10% of book value.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: Thin and honestly labeled: no information edge (the 8-K is public). The residual is structural — income funds exited on the dividend suspension while the buyback replaces the return more tax-efficiently, and the multi-state book gets lumped with pure-Florida peers.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: The market is already pricing the normalization (that's the -8.4% YTD); our +25% base case needs the quiet season to actually happen.
edge_explainer.what_resolves_it: Q2 print Aug-11 (first quarter on the new cost basis — NEP lift visible or not); then the Aug-Oct season peak; Q3 print completes it.
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: NEP failing to rise while combined ratio holds = the givebacks are outrunning the saving = the bulge never existed — exit, don't wait for the wind.
edge_explainer.edge_type: RP_FAIR carry + dated catalysts; starter at market per taxonomy (business risks are carried by SIZE)
